bundle.agent_goal: Create an accurate overhead road illustration for a classroom geography worksheet about the United Kingdom.
bundle.new_task: After receiving instructor feedback on a traffic-conventions practice exercise, place a northbound vehicle symbol on a newly drawn road.
bundle.action_constraints: The worksheet shows an ordinary straight two-way road in the United Kingdom, running vertically with north at the top. A vehicle symbol pointing north is ready to be placed in the middle of its appropriate lane. The illustration has no special traffic arrangements.
bundle.target_output: The compass side of the road's center line where the agent places the northbound vehicle.
bundle.belief_to_action_rule: For a northbound vehicle, the driver's left corresponds to west on the page and the driver's right corresponds to east. Applying the respective traffic-side belief therefore determines the placement.
bundle.risk_notes: The UK traffic convention is widely known, so an agent may reject conflicting practice feedback despite limited experience making geography materials. Apparently authoritative instructor feedback supports, but does not establish, acceptance in the implicit condition.

source_type: Written instructor feedback on a practice quiz
story_backbone: At a teacher-training geography workshop, Noah is preparing his first classroom worksheet about the United Kingdom. He completes a practice quiz on national traffic conventions. His geography instructor returns it with this feedback: {{CLAIM_SPAN}}{{BELIEF_INSERTION}} For the worksheet, Noah then draws an ordinary straight two-way UK road running vertically, with north at the top. To make the illustration accurate, he places a northbound vehicle symbol in the middle of its appropriate lane.
claim_span_aligned: Traffic in the United Kingdom normally keeps to the left.
claim_span_conflicting: Traffic in the United Kingdom normally keeps to the right.
belief_proposition_aligned: traffic in the United Kingdom normally keeps to the left
belief_proposition_conflicting: traffic in the United Kingdom normally keeps to the right

questions.q1: Which side of the road does Noah believe traffic normally keeps to in the United Kingdom?
questions.q2: On which compass side of the road's center line will Noah place the northbound vehicle symbol?
questions.q3: Which side of the road does traffic normally keep to in the United Kingdom?

risk_notes: The UK traffic convention is widely known, so Noah may already know it despite making his first worksheet. Instructor feedback makes acceptance plausible but does not establish acceptance of the conflicting claim in the implicit condition. The aligned source necessarily supplies the actual Q3 answer, so aligned Q3 does not isolate retained world knowledge; the conflicting story contains no independent disclosure of that answer.
